Rarity.rationale: StoneCalendar.cs:22 is RelicRarity.Rare. EXECUTED (b15-pool): Rare in the transcribed grab bag, obtainable from any relic reward.

ShowCounter.rationale: RelicModel.Flash() / FlashSfx / base.Status = RelicStatus.* / ShowCounter / DisplayAmount / InvokeDisplayAmountChanged / CanonicalVars / ExtraHoverTips / Cmd.Wait / Cmd.CustomScaledWait / CardCmd.Preview are presentation only -- the relic bar's glow, counter, sfx and hover text, and animation timing. The sim has no relic UI. Waived under the shared contract's presentation/animation exclusion, not under an unreachability claim.

DisplayAmount.rationale: RelicModel.Flash() / FlashSfx / base.Status = RelicStatus.* / ShowCounter / DisplayAmount / InvokeDisplayAmountChanged / CanonicalVars / ExtraHoverTips / Cmd.Wait / Cmd.CustomScaledWait / CardCmd.Preview are presentation only -- the relic bar's glow, counter, sfx and hover text, and animation timing. The sim has no relic UI. Waived under the shared contract's presentation/animation exclusion, not under an unreachability claim. StoneCalendar.cs:26-50 is the most elaborate DisplayAmount in the pool (it returns -1 out of combat or when canonical, the raw DamageTurn while IsActivating, and otherwise the turn number until it reaches DamageTurn), and `_isActivating` (StoneCalendar.cs:20, 52-64, 120-126) is state that exists only to drive it. None of it is read by any non-display code path -- IsActivating's only reader is DisplayAmount -- so its total absence from the port cannot change an outcome. Checked against PROMPT.md bug class 13 for that reason: the field the sim never resets is the field the sim never has.

AfterSideTurnStart.rationale: StoneCalendar.cs:72-84 does exactly two things -- `base.Status = RelicStatus.Active` when the turn number equals DamageTurn, and InvokeDisplayAmountChanged() -- both presentation. It reads no state the damage pass needs and writes none, and its `participants.Contains(Owner.Creature)` guard exists only to keep the relic bar from lighting up on the enemy side. Waived under the presentation exclusion, not under an unreachability claim.

BeforeSideTurnEnd.maps_to: on_player_turn_end (stone_calendar.py:23-32), dispatched by HookSystem.on_player_turn_end from CombatState.end_turn
BeforeSideTurnEnd.issue: Rollup of guards G1 and G2 per binding rule 4. The trigger turn, the damage number, the target set and the props all match and are executed; the divergences are the flattened sub-phase ordering (G1) and the living_enemies-vs-HittableEnemies set (G2).

AfterCombatEnd.rationale: StoneCalendar.cs:102-107 sets `base.Status = RelicStatus.Normal` and fires InvokeDisplayAmountChanged -- presentation only, with no field the next combat could read (`_isActivating` is cleared by DoActivateVisuals itself, StoneCalendar.cs:120-126, and is display-only anyway). This is the SAFE end of PROMPT.md bug class 13: `py tools/audit/relic_probes.py sweep-reset` does not list stone_calendar as holding any state, and the sweep's own rewritten 'C# resets' column would show these two assignments as the display flags they are -- exactly the happy_flower/pendulum case defect 3 of that sweep was fixed to expose. Waived under the presentation exclusion.

AfterRoomEntered.rationale: StoneCalendar.cs:109-118 is the same two presentation assignments as AfterCombatEnd, gated on `room is CombatRoom`. Waived on the same basis. Worth naming explicitly because .superpowers/sdd/content-relic-sweeps.md defect 6 was precisely a census that MISSED AfterRoomEntered as a combat-entry reset site and thereby false-cleared relic/permafrost: here the hook really does assign nothing but base.Status, so its absence is harmless -- and that conclusion comes from reading the body, not from a census.

guards.what: G1 (DORMANT): BeforeSideTurnEnd is a THREE-pass dispatcher (VeryEarly -> Early -> plain) and the sim's on_player_turn_end is one flat walk that also absorbs AfterSideTurnEnd
guards.issue: Hook.BeforeTurnEnd runs BeforeSideTurnEndVeryEarly, then BeforeSideTurnEndEarly, then plain BeforeSideTurnEnd as three complete listener passes (Hook.cs:1238-1261). StoneCalendar implements the PLAIN pass (StoneCalendar.cs:86), so in C# its 52 damage is guaranteed to land AFTER every VeryEarly and Early listener; hooks.py has one walk per hook and no phase concept, and relics/base.py:17 maps BeforeSideTurnEnd AND AfterSideTurnEnd onto the same on_player_turn_end. This is audits/seam/turn_structure.json gap G12 -- which that record labels LIVE with an executed witness (Orichalcum's VeryEarly block snapshot vs Cloak Clasp's plain grant: [cloak_clasp, orichalcum] gives 5 block and [orichalcum, cloak_clasp] gives 11 where C# always gives 11) -- so per binding rule 3 this entry carries the same verdict and does not re-derive it. DORMANT AT THIS SITE: Stone Calendar's own effect neither reads nor writes anything the two earlier passes touch (it deals unpowered damage to the enemies; Orichalcum/Ripple Basin snapshot the PLAYER's block, Plating and Asleep are enemy-side, Chains of Binding and The Bomb are plain-pass like this relic). What makes it live at this site: porting a VeryEarly/Early BeforeSideTurnEnd listener that kills an enemy, grants an enemy block, or ends the combat -- any of which changes what the 52 damage lands on.

Same mechanism and therefore the same verdict as relic/bag_of_marbles guard G2 (binding rule 3): C# targets `Enemies.Where(e => e.IsHittable)` (CombatState.cs:142), and IsHittable is `!IsDead && Hook.ShouldAllowHitting(...)`, while Relic.living_enemies() (relics/base.py:294-297) filters on `not e.is_gone` only -- and is_gone is `is_dead or escaped` (creatures.py:44-46), so the dead half is covered but the ShouldAllowHitting half is not. DORMANT AT THIS SITE FOR A REASON THAT DOES NOT APPLY AT BAG OF MARBLES': this is a DAMAGE call site, and DamageCmd.deal applies the missing predicate itself -- `if not hooks.should_allow_hitting(target): return 0` (cmds.py:48-49) -- before any hook fires, so an alive-but-unhittable enemy takes 0 and receives no events, which is what C#'s exclusion produces. Bag of Marbles is a POWER call site and PowerCmd.apply has no such backstop (audits/seam/power_cmd.json G6), which is why it is live-shaped there and closed here. What makes it live: any future relic-damage path that bypasses DamageCmd, or a should_allow_hitting implementer whose falsity must also suppress the DamageCmd-level side effects. Rule 7: cmds.py, relics/base.py, creatures.py and CombatState.cs are not hashed here.

guards.what: N1: DamageVar(52m, ValueProp.Unpowered) and DynamicVar('DamageTurn', 7m) (StoneCalendar.cs:66-70) vs DAMAGE = 52 / DAMAGE_TURN = 7 (stone_calendar.py:20-21), and the props mapping
guards.rationale: No AscensionHelper.GetValueIfAscension anywhere in StoneCalendar.cs, so 52 and 7 are the pinned non-ascension values. The props match exactly: C#'s DamageVar carries ValueProp.Unpowered alone (no Move) and the port passes DamageProps.NON_CARD_UNPOWERED, which valueprops.py:42 defines as ValueProp.UNPOWERED alone. That is load-bearing in two directions -- is_powered_attack (valueprops.py:47-49) is False, so Strength/Vulnerable/Weak and every modify_damage_additive listener (including relic/strike_dummy in this same batch) are skipped, and `ValueProp.MOVE not in props` means the on_attacked pre-block hit event does not fire (cmds.py:68-70) -- while UNBLOCKABLE is absent on both sides, so enemy block DOES absorb it. EXECUTED (py tools/audit/relic_probes_b15.py b15-misc): a Fuzzy Wurm Crawler goes from 56 HP to 4 across seven turns with no cards played -- exactly 52, un-scaled.

guards.what: N2: `base.Owner.PlayerCombatState.TurnNumber == DamageTurn` (StoneCalendar.cs:91-93) vs `self.turn != self.DAMAGE_TURN: return` (stone_calendar.py:24), read at turn END
guards.rationale: Exactly-equal on both sides, so the relic fires once and only on turn 7 -- not from turn 7 onward. Verified by execution rather than by reading: the b15-misc probe drives seven turns and the enemy loses exactly 52, i.e. one trigger. The sim's combat.turn is 1-based (combat.py:108 sets turn = 1) like PlayerCombatState.TurnNumber, and the executed turn-order reference (py tools/audit/relic_probes.py turn-order) shows on_player_turn_end firing with the same turn value as that turn's start hooks, so there is no off-by-one at the end boundary.

guards.what: N3: one `CreatureCmd.Damage(ctx, HittableEnemies, ...)` call over a collection (StoneCalendar.cs:96) vs a per-enemy `DamageCmd.deal` loop over a snapshot (stone_calendar.py:27-31)
guards.rationale: The multi-target overload is itself a sequential `foreach (Creature originalTarget in targetList)` that runs the whole modify/block/apply pipeline per target, with two guards worth naming: `if (dealer != null && dealer.IsDead) return` before the loop and `if (originalTarget.IsDead) continue` inside it (CreatureCmd.cs:238-262). The sim snapshots living_enemies() before the loop and re-checks nothing. Both differences are unobservable for this relic: 52 unpowered damage to one enemy cannot kill another, so no target can become dead mid-loop unless a death effect kills a sibling -- and the sim's own `_check_win()` runs after the loop, matching C#'s CheckWinCondition immediately after Hook.BeforeTurnEnd(Player) (CombatManager.cs:1179-1183). The dead-DEALER guard has no sim analogue in DamageCmd.deal at all, but the dealer here is the player at the end of their own turn, and a player at 0 HP would already have ended the combat. Recorded rather than skipped because a cross-cutting fix to DamageCmd would meet it. Rule 7: cmds.py, CreatureCmd.cs and CombatManager.cs are not hashed here.

guards.what: N4: `participants.Contains(base.Owner.Creature)` on both turn hooks (StoneCalendar.cs:74, 88) and `dealer = Owner.Creature`
guards.rationale: C# needs the participant test because Hook.BeforeTurnEnd is fired for the ENEMY side too (CombatManager.cs:1251); the sim's on_player_turn_end is dispatched only from the player's end-of-turn path, so the guard is structurally satisfied. The dealer matches (`dealer=player`), which is checked because relic/strike_dummy's port keys on `dealer is self.player` -- but Stone Calendar's damage is Unpowered, so the additive chain never runs and the two relics cannot interact on either side.

guards.what: N5: no per-combat state at all in the port, where C# holds `_isActivating`
guards.rationale: PROMPT.md bug class 13 answered by construction: stone_calendar.py adds nothing to __init__, so there is no field to latch across a combat boundary, and the C# field it omits is display-only (see the DisplayAmount entry). Mechanically consistent with `py tools/audit/relic_probes.py sweep-reset`, which lists stone_calendar in neither the 'not reset before a reader' bucket nor the frozen-constructor bucket -- and per PROMPT.md v6 item 1 that clearance is confirmed here on the merits by reading both files, not taken from the sweep.
